sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45-92. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210 (open access).
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.1 Phonology (pp. 54-58) describes only ɛBoze as the exemplar ('All East Kainji languages so far studied have a relatively simple phonology and broadly resemble one another'); tones: Boze has four level tones plus glides; 'Other East Kainji languages have much reduced systems... Shimizu (1979, 1982a) usually transcribes the tonal systems in his lists as High and Low or High, Low and Downstep'. Sanga appears only in Table 1 (p. 49, status 'Vigorous', source column empty), the Fig. 5 tree (Lemoro-Sanga node) and Table 12 ('arm/hand' ò-ʔàra / tà-ʔàra). The word 'stress' occurs now…
